result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, the credential-sync branch returns a raw fetch Response (from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) directly, whereas the normal branch returns the provider-specific result (Google's myGoogleAuth.refreshToken returns an object with a .data property). Google CalendarService then does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` — a Response object has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. This is visible directly in the diff and breaks token refresh when credential sharing is enabled.

judged_text: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the following line reads res?.data, which is undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh for a self-hoster with credential sync enabled crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' instead of refreshing the token, breaking the exact workflow this PR ships.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a raw `Response`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` but `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when credential sync is enabled.
